chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from Abdullah ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The waiting period of the woman who gives Khul'a is the waiting period of the divorced woman, and her Khul'a is her divorce.
He said: And I asked him, 'Does she receive something (as maintenance during the waiting period)?' He said: 'No'.

key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِعَةِ: The woman who gives Khul'a (divorce by compensation)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period and maintenance status for a woman who divorces her husband through Khul'a?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the Khul'a mechanism is legally treated as a revocable divorce (Talaq), thereby imposing the standard waiting period (Iddah) and terminating the husband's obligation to provide maintenance (Nafaqah) during that time. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that Khul'a is a form of dissolution initiated by the wife but carrying the same legal consequences as a husband-initiated divorce, distinguishing it from other forms of separation.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from Muhammad Bin Ziyad, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
A waiting period of the woman divorced by Al-Khul’a is a waiting period of the divorced woman, and her Khul’a is her divorce’.
And I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Would she be provided with something?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 5. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from Muhammad ibn Ziyad from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that waiting period for a woman in al-Khul‘ is like that of a divorced woman and her al-Khul‘ is her divorce.’
He (the narrator) has said that he then asked if she receives any benefits.
He (the Imam) said, ‘No, she does not receive any benefits.’”
